key_insight: ASH learns an activation steering vector that reproduces hint-induced model behavior at inference without requiring hints in the input.
engineering_relevance: ASH offers a way to address sparse-reward reasoning training while reducing the training–inference context mismatch of hint-augmented GRPO.
method: Train with both hinted and plain versions of questions.
Optimize a steering vector to widen response-probability margins between hinted and plain inputs, capturing shared hint-induced behavior.
Inject the learned vector into model activations at inference without adding textual hints.
evidence_signal: Across four Qwen3 and Llama-3.2 models, ASH consistently improves pass@k on competition-math and out-of-distribution benchmarks, with reported average pass@8 gains of 2.60% and 2.21% for Qwen3-1.7B-Base and Qwen3-4B-Base.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify activation injection locations or steering overhead, leaving implementation cost and sensitivity unclear.
paper_title: Get Hint-Augmented GRPO Done Right Through Activation Steering
